Answer: C
Reason: The axial CT images show a large posterior mediastinal mass that surrounds the descending aorta (visible as a contrast-filled circle within the soft tissue density) without obliterating its lumen, indicating the vessel remains patent. This "encasing" appearance is characteristic of certain posterior mediastinal tumors (like neurogenic tumors) which tend to displace or surround structures rather than invade them early on.
